options.text: Construct an equilateral triangle from equal-radius arcs to obtain a $60^{\circ}$ angle at $P$.
Name ray $PQ$ as the finished $15^{\circ}$ angle.
Draw a $45^{\circ}$ angle at $P$ as the starting angle.
Bisect a $15^{\circ}$ angle to create the equal-radius arcs.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

stem: Vikram must construct an exact $15^{\circ}$ angle at point $P$ on ray $PQ$, using equal-radius arcs and angle bisection.

part_answers.answer: Equal-radius arcs make an equilateral triangle, so a $60^{\circ}$ angle appears at $P$; that angle is then bisected to $30^{\circ}$ and again to $15^{\circ}$.

teacher.key_rationale: Start with a 60° equilateral construction at P, then bisect twice to 15°. Naming ray PQ as 15° swaps the term. Starting at 45° leaves the 60–30–15 path. Bisecting 15° to create the arcs reverses the construction order.
